criteria.criterion: The diff only moves code: no function body in the moved items changes, and the public names (boundary_words, boundary_fragments, boundary_scan, plain_boundary_text, BoundaryHit, and the instruction constants) remain reachable at athena_context::briefs::.

The only edits are `banned_words_section` becoming `pub(super)`, and tab indentation on the continuation lines of BOUNDARY_SCAN_INSTRUCTION. In Rust a trailing `\` in a string skips the leading whitespace (tabs included) of the next line, so the string's value is unchanged. `pub use boundary::{BOUNDARY_SCAN_INSTRUCTION, BoundaryHit, boundary_fragments, boundary_scan, boundary_words, plain_boundary_text}` keeps the public paths. findings.summary: The plan was sized from the request's quoted figure instead of measuring the file
findings.evidence: The reading's code survey records the test module at line 2545, which implies about 2544 production lines, yet it planned around 1524. Measuring with athena_core::code_health::measure_source, which `athena status` shows, would have shown that one 270-line move cannot reach 1500. A correct approach would split briefs.rs along several responsibilities, for example per-role brief rendering, and would also break up the function over 200 lines.

summary: The candidate cleanly moves the boundary-scan group (boundary_words through plain_boundary_text) out of crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs into briefs/boundary.rs. It re-exports the public names, leaves the tests untouched, and the recorded fmt, clippy and test checks pass. But it does not do what the request asked: bring briefs.rs under its code-health limit. Athena's own code-health table (`athena status` on this tree) measures the candidate's briefs.rs at 2287 production lines with a longest function of 217 lines. The test module starts at line 2288 and runs to line 5095. The base file had 2544 production lines (its test module started at line 2545, as the reading itself notes). So moving about 257 lines leaves the file above the 1500 busy-file limit and even above the 2000-line hard limit, and one function is still over the 200-line limit. Criterion 1 is unmet, so the verdict is fail. The request quotes 1524 production lines, but the snapshot base does not match that figure. The plan relied on the request's number instead of measuring the file.
